outcome: Mode of delivery (Cesarean section, Vaginal delivery)
cohort: Pregnant women diagnosed with Subchorionic hematoma (SCH), predominantly in their mid-twenties to early thirties, with a balanced representation of primiparous and multiparous women.
finding: The study described the demographic and clinical characteristics of pregnant women with SCH, finding significant associations between SCH size and vaginal bleeding/previous abortion history, and noting an incidence of maternal complications and low birth weight among fetal outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was found to be more common than vaginal delivery in women with SCH.
